description:
November 19, 2026: GTA 6 is scheduled to launch. What happens to the world when millions of people press start at the same time?

In this video: a launch wave across time zones (real NASA night-lights data), the lines outside stores, the trailer's YouTube record (90.4 million views in 24 hours, a Guinness-recognised record for a game reveal), the money benchmark (GTA 5: $800 million on day one, $1 billion in three days), the "blast zone" publishers avoid, servers, streamers, and the world of Leonida.

Facts and caveats:
- Release date: November 19, 2026 (official). The launch hour is NOT announced by Rockstar; PlayStation Store listings reportedly point to a rolling unlock at local midnight, New Zealand first and the last region about 19 hours later (GamesRadar / Kotaku, Sept 2026). The launch-wave map follows that reported rollout.
- GTA 5 sales: Take-Two reported $800M in the first 24 hours and $1B in three days (September 2013) and over 200 million copies lifetime.
- "Blast zone" is a term used in industry reporting (The Game Business) for the weeks around a launch when publishers avoid release dates. The calendar graphic is an illustration, no real release dates are shown.
- Nobody outside Take-Two knows GTA 6 sales numbers yet; analyst forecasts differ widely, so none are used here.
- Lines such as "expect servers to brace" are expectations, not reports.

All game-style frames and clips are AI-generated concept art, NOT game footage. The night-lights map is real data (NASA VIIRS). Voice-over and music are synthetic/original. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two.

Where will you be at midnight on November 19? Tell me below 👇

Most people mix up the UAE, Abu Dhabi and Dubai. Here's the difference in one minute.

The UAE is one country of seven emirates, about 83,000 km² (roughly the size of Austria). Each emirate has its own ruler. Abu Dhabi is the biggest emirate, with about 85% of the land, and its city is the capital. Dubai is a different emirate, home of the Burj Khalifa and the Palm islands.
